README: The report guard's LANGUAGE, as data. `report_guard.py` keeps the position/shape machinery
— anchors count only at the head of a line, sentences are split the same way, tiers are
decided the same way — and reads every STRING it matches from here.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every anchor and every lexicon below is English. A final report
written in another language matches no anchor and no progress word, so it is neither a
hand-off nor mid-flow: the guard blocks it demanding an anchor it cannot express, three
times, and then stands down. The regexes do not learn every language; a deployment
SAYS what its anchors are.
HOW TO ADD A LOCALE. Copy an `en` block under the same command (and under `shared`), give it
your locale's key, and translate the strings. Every locale present is read: the anchors are
UNIONED, so an English hand-off and a Hebrew one both land, and a mixed-language session
keeps working. Nothing here is keyed to the session's language — a locale is accepted, never
required.
SHAPES. `anchors` and `progress_anchors` are LITERAL strings matched at a LINE HEAD, followed
by the skeleton's separator — ANY punctuation, so write your locale's own: `スイート: 検証済み。`
and `…（7件）` land the same way `Run complete —` does. A separator is still required there: an
anchor running straight on into prose is a sentence, not a skeleton line.
`contact_anchor`, `capacity_anchor` and `unavailable_anchor` are literal strings too, each the WHOLE FIRST SENTENCE,
final punctuation included, of one of the plugin's three stop texts (the contact hand-off, the capacity stop, the
unavailable stop), and they are matched by a DIFFERENT rule — do not write them as a skeleton line with a separator.
Each counts only at a LINE HEAD, after the optional decoration a skeleton line allows (`> `, `**`, `- `) and an
optional short bold label (`**Stopped:** `), with nothing else before it on the line, case insensitively, and the
sentence must END there: closing emphasis, then whitespace or the line's end (after a full stop like `。` that takes no
space, the next sentence may follow at once). A line that opens like the sentence and runs on (`…right now, so I'll
retry`) is narration, not a stop. What follows the first sentence is not compared, so a linked email or a
blockquote still lands. A stop text inside a sentence of prose is not a stop, and neither is a message that carries
its command's report anchor (a finished report that quotes a scenario row; the anchor may sit above or below the text;
the stop's own done lines and, below the text, a command's `floor_anchors` entry — the line a failed flow's skeleton
ends on — do not count). The unavailable stop records the same liftable `capacity` halt as the capacity stop. The
kinds are tried in a fixed order: the capacity sentence, then the unavailable one, then the contact one, then the credit
substring. A message that prints two stop texts reads as the first kind in that order, and a credit stop that prints
the contact text at a line head reads as contact unless the run's plan recorded the halt's kind as the stop printed,
which wins. Write the first sentence of the text your locale's
stop actually prints. A report that quotes a stop row above its floor line reads as a stop, so a flow whose failure
skeleton ends on a floor line must not quote a stop text above it.
`credit_anchor` is the sentence that follows every credit kind's own sentence (the kinds' sentences differ, that one does
not). It keeps the substring rule: lowercased and looked for ANYWHERE in the message. The `credit-unavailable` kind prints the
contact text alone, so its text reads as the contact stop; the halt the printing script records for it is the
liftable `capacity` kind.
Everything else is a REGULAR EXPRESSION in
Python syntax; the shared lexicons are matched case-insensitively, and a command's `stem` is
matched line-anchored with `stem_ignorecase` deciding its case sensitivity.
WHAT EACH LEXICON DECIDES. `completion` + `stem`: does this message read as the command's
final hand-off, so it OWES the anchor. `progress`: does it read as live progress, so it earns
the relaxed mid-flow tier. `abort`: is it a unilateral early stop. `abort_reason`: the part of
`abort` that names a timing/context/budget REASON — the only part still checked on a failure
hand-off, whose job 'stopped before it could finish' is the failure itself. `run_integrity`: is it
doctrine item 4's licensed result line (which the gap and abort rules must NOT catch).
`eval_fitness_subject` + `eval_fitness_claim`, both required in ONE sentence: is it an
eval-set fitness caveat, which no anchor licenses. `result_doubt`: does it hand the reader the
product's confidence in its own result, which stays in the internal files.
An anchor a skill's report skeleton does not render is an anchor no message can carry: change
the skeleton and this file together.
